questions.q: What happens to a tabular report when you add a row grouping in the Outline panel?
options: It stays tabular but gets a new sort order
It is deleted and must be rebuilt
It becomes a summary report with subtotals per group
questions.explain: Groupings are what distinguish summary reports from tabular ones; adding a row grouping converts the report to summary (and a column grouping too makes it a matrix).

questions.q: You want one line per group showing counts and totals, without the individual records underneath. What do you use?
questions.explain: Turning off Show Details hides the detail rows and leaves group headings with their summary values, the closest native equivalent to a GROUP BY result.

questions.q: Why is grouping directly by a raw Close Date field usually a poor choice for a trend report?
options: Date fields cannot be grouped in Salesforce
It creates one group per distinct day; a coarser Group Date By such as Month or Quarter is more useful
It forces the report into matrix format
questions.explain: Grouping by the raw date yields one group per day. Group Date By options such as Month, Calendar Quarter, or Fiscal Quarter give readable trends.

questions.q: Roughly how many levels of row grouping does a summary report allow in the Lightning report builder, per this lesson?
questions.explain: A summary report supports up to three row groupings; a matrix supports up to two row and two column groupings.

questions.q: A report page shows only a capped number of detail rows on screen. What is true about the totals?
options: They only count the rows displayed
They are hidden whenever the cap is hit
They still reflect all matching records
questions.explain: The on-screen detail is capped (around 2,000 rows in the Lightning run page), but summaries and totals are calculated over every matching record.
